purpose: Attribute the frozen full multimodal model's outputs to its 62 input features (50 PAM50 genes + 12 clinical features).

data.preprocessing: Train-fold statistics carried inside the checkpoint; nothing was refitted for this analysis.

1_model_in_eval_mode.note: Dropout and any train-time behaviour are disabled.

2_no_optimizer_step.note: No torch.optim object exists in this script. Expected gradients use torch.autograd.grad, which does not accumulate into .grad or modify weights.

6_no_test_labels_used_for_shap.method: re-encoded the same patients with all targets blanked

modality_contribution.note: Shares compare the two modalities within one shared 62-feature attribution space. The genomic block has 50 features and the clinical block 12, so a larger genomic total partly reflects that width; the per-feature means in the table are the fairer feature-level comparison.

interpretation.shap_values_are: model-attribution values describing how this trained model distributes its own output across its own inputs
shap_values_are_not: a basis for any clinical decision
interpretation.pam50_framing: The PAM50 task is reproduction/recovery of the established PAM50 assignment from the same 50-gene panel that assignment derives from. High attribution to PAM50 genes is therefore expected by construction and is not independent molecular-subtype discovery.
interpretation.additivity: Expected gradients is a sampling approximation, so the per-patient SHAP sum only approximately equals f(x) - E[f(background)]. The recorded additivity gap quantifies that approximation; it is a diagnostic, not an error.
